title: Contributor onboarding, lightweight RFCs, and phased retirement playbook for tokens & components
creator: Evelyn Park
description: Goal: Establish a pragmatic playbook that standardizes contributor onboarding, a lightweight RFC process, review checklist, and a phased retirement (sunset) workflow for design tokens and core components (buttons, tables, charts). Rationale: recurring uncoordinated changes to tokens and shared components cause regressions, unexpected consumption spikes, and increased maintenance. The playbook should reduce reviewer overhead, provide predictable timelines for breaking changes, and include automation touchpoints (codemods, telemetry, migration guides). Scope: tokens, atomic components (buttons, inputs), data components (tables, charts), and shared utilities (spacing, color tokens). Out of scope: one-off product-specific component forks and platform infra-only changes. Deliverables: 1) Contributor onboarding checklist and quickstart templates; 2) Lightweight RFC template + triage rubric; 3) Review checklist covering accessibility, tokens, visual diff expectations, performance, and backward-compatibility; 4) Phased retirement workflow with timelines, migration resources, deprecation headers, and automation plan; 5) Owner matrix and escalation path; 6) Example RFCs and migration PR templates.
acceptance_criteria: A clear CONTRIBUTING.md onboarding section exists and is linkable from token/component repos
A one-page lightweight RFC template is published and used for any API or token changes that can break consumers
Review checklist integrated into PR template and accessible in the design handbook
Deprecation workflow defines three phases (announce, soft-deprecate with automations, removal) and example timelines
At least one codemod plan and migration guide exists for a sample token rename and a table prop change
Owners for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts are listed and an escalation flow is documented
